episode.subject: pygmy seahorses on a sea fan
episode.title: A tail beside mine
episode.body: He curled his tail near mine. I moved a little closer, then spent a ridiculous amount of time pretending to inspect the branch between us.

proposals.visibleScene: Two grey seahorses with red tubercles occupy adjacent branches of a red sea fan. Foreground animal faces down-left with a clearly curled tail toward upper-right. Second animal faces up-left and is partly obscured by branches. They are close within the same branch network; no tail-to-tail contact or copulation is claimed.
proposals.fictionBoundary: Cast foreground animal as female Dot and upper-left companion as male. Photograph does not establish sex, reproductive condition, relationship, movement sequence or intention. Curled-tail approach, Dot moving closer and feigned inspection are fiction around the visible proximity. No pregnancy or egg transfer is asserted.
proposals.continuity: Recover original slot 7, preserving all ten existing titles and bodies, Dot female canon, avatar and Misool home. Original slot follows The full distance and precedes later held Leave a little grip. This does not bind any other held scene. Source provenance says Indonesia, not specifically Misool; illustration does not establish a journey or precise canon location.
proposals.authorReview: The turn is desire followed by an unconvincing cover activity. It differs from A little too secure, where a tail betrays fear of losing grip, and The full distance, about routes and panic. Two visible animals earn a stronger pairing than a solitary portrait. The second body is partly hidden and its tail is not wholly traceable; independent lead should decide whether proximity is sufficiently legible. Do not expand this into documented mating behavior.
proposals.biologyEvidence: Australian Museum independently opened: H. bargibanti lives on Muricella sea fans and grips with a prehensile tail; grey/purple bodies with pink/red tubercles are described. This supports body and substrate compatibility, not sex identification or photographed courtship.
